phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Core Independent Implementation Verification
summary: Phase 147H independently verified the Phase 147G implementation of pcae.authority_evaluation against AEMIC-001 v1.2, treating implementation, tests, and canonical report as untrusted claims. Read AEMIC-001 v1.2 in full and independently reconstructed the public model, seven-parameter evaluate() signature, field sources, exception hierarchy, error-precedence ordering, Registry ABC boundary, serialization rules, and forbidden-dependency list before reading Phase 147G's own test file. Disclosed two authorization-prompt premise mismatches: the phantom model names AuthorityEvaluationRequest and RegistryResolution (neither exists in AEM-001, AEMIC-001, or the code -- AEMIC-REQ-019 explicitly rejects a request-wrapper object), and a claimed 'Commits: PENDING' finalization-state text with no match anywhere in this repository's git history. Wrote 90 new independent adversarial tests in tests/test_phase_147h_authority_evaluation_independent_verification.py -- no shared fixtures or test doubles with Phase 147G's own 93 -- covering evaluator-signature introspection, an 11-case exception-precedence adversarial matrix (including Unicode-lookalike and case/whitespace template-identity attacks), the citation_text if-and-only-if invariant at both evaluate() and constructor level, AuthorityRegistry ABC isolation via five independently-written test doubles, serialization adversarial cases, determinism under repetition/independent-equal-inputs/16-thread concurrency, equality/hashing, disclosure-only security behaviorally verified, and forbidden dependencies checked both statically (AST) and dynamically (import side effects). All 90 pass; Phase 147G's own 93 still pass unmodified. Independently built a wheel and sdist in an isolated venv (the sandboxed system Python's own pip refuses --break-system-packages) and confirmed both archives contain all six authority_evaluation modules, directly demonstrating rather than merely asserting no packaging omission exists. Confirmed the fast_green tier identical at 4391/4391. A full ~27,000-test whole-suite run was attempted four times (single-process and -n auto, at current HEAD and at an isolated git worktree of Phase 147G's own parent commit) and was terminated each time by this sandbox's own execution-time limit before completion; substituted an exact test-collection-count reconciliation (27026 minus 26843 equals exactly 93 plus 90, zero collection errors) plus individual, both-commits reproduction of every specific pre-existing-failure category Phase 147G's own report names (wheel/sdist packaging, advisory-runtime directory-shape, finalization-ordering, rendering regression, tasks/TODO.md staleness) -- each reproduces identically at the parent commit, confirming none is a regression this phase's predecessor caused. Reassessed BF-147F-1, BF-147F.1-1, F-147F.1-2, F-147F.1-3, and F-147F.1-4: each confirmed either correctly implemented or correctly still-open exactly as previously disclosed. Raised one new Informational finding: declaration_from_payload accepts a dict (silently reduced to its own key set) rather than requiring a JSON array for eligible_identities -- not a contract violation, named for a future hardening pass. Overall Verdict: AUTHORITY EVALUATION MODEL IMPLEMENTATION VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147H_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_CORE_INDEPENDENT_IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION.md.
tests_added_or_updated: Added tests/test_phase_147h_authority_evaluation_independent_verification.py (90 new, independent tests). No existing test file, including tests/test_phase_147g_authority_evaluation.py, was modified.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_contract_reconstruction
validation_results.result: Read AEMIC-001 v1.2 in full (2407 lines, all sections through the end) before reading tests/test_phase_147g_authority_evaluation.py, independently deriving the public model set (three types, one function, one ABC, nine exceptions -- fourteen names total per AEMIC-REQ-014), the seven-parameter evaluate() signature, the six-step error-precedence ordering, and the field-source matrix directly from AEMIC-001's own requirement text.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_premise_verification
validation_results.result: Confirmed AuthorityEvaluationRequest and RegistryResolution do not exist anywhere in AEM-001, AEMIC-001, or the implementation (grep across both contract files finds AuthorityEvaluationRequest only as an explicitly rejected §25 candidate, and RegistryResolution nowhere at all); confirmed the literal string 'Commits: PENDING' does not appear anywhere in this repository's git history via git log -p --all -S; both disclosed as authorization-prompt premise mismatches rather than silently substituted.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_signature_and_precedence_verification
validation_results.result: TestEvaluatorSignatureIntrospection (5 tests) confirms the exact seven-parameter signature via inspect.signature. TestExceptionPrecedenceIndependentMatrix (11 tests) independently attacks double- and triple-simultaneous-violation inputs and confirms the first-ordered failure always wins, including a case (mismatch beats missing-citation) not named by Phase 147G's own four precedence tests.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_template_identity_and_citation_verification
validation_results.result: TestTemplateIdentityAgreementAdversarial (9 tests) confirms exact-match/mismatch/Unicode-lookalike/case/whitespace behavior. TestCitationInvariantAdversarial (9 tests) confirms the if-and-only-if invariant at both evaluate() and direct AuthorityEvaluationOutcome construction, and reconfirms F-147F.1-2 (empty-string citation) and F-147F.1-3 (non-string citation typing) remain open and unaffected by Phase 147G.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_registry_isolation_verification
validation_results.result: TestAuthorityRegistryABCIsolation (8 tests, five independently-written test doubles distinct from Phase 147G's own three) confirms the ABC cannot be instantiated, exposes exactly one abstract method, has no write method, and registry.py's own module source (via ast.parse) defines exactly one class.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_serialization_determinism_hashing_verification
validation_results.result: TestSerializationAdversarial (12 tests), TestDeterminismIndependent (6 tests including a 16-thread concurrency test), and TestEqualityAndHashingIndependent (6 tests) independently confirm round-trip correctness including Unicode, schema-version-first checking, if-and-only-if enforcement on the deserialization path, deterministic repeatability, and equal-hashes-for-equal-objects. Raised one new Informational finding: declaration_from_payload silently accepts a dict for eligible_identities (reduced to its key set) rather than only a JSON array -- not a contract violation.

validation_results.name: phase_147h_forbidden_dependency_and_disclosure_verification
validation_results.result: TestForbiddenDependenciesIndependent (parametrized over all six package files, plus 2 tests) independently confirms via AST, not text search, that no forbidden root is imported statically or as a runtime side effect. TestDisclosureOnlySecurityBehavioral (4 tests) independently confirms disclosure-only naming and behavior, including that importing the package performs no filesystem write.
